items.title: Diamond Foundry creates world's first 200mm single-crystal diamond wafer
items.description: This 200mm single-crystal diamond wafer is designed to efficiently remove heat and prevent hotspots from forming on AI processors.
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 3 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Diamonds have exceptional cooling capabilities due to their excellent thermal conductivity, with the material estimated to be at least five times more conductive than copper. Because of this, Diamond Foundry, a firm focusing on lab-grown diamonds, announced the world’s first 200mm single-crystal diamond (SCD) wafer. The 200mm SCD is about the same wafer size that semiconductor fabs use for older processes, with the company boasting on its website that “Single-crystal diamond has entered the wafer-scale era.” This is part of the effort to manufacture SCD at scale so that it can be used for semiconductor cooling, especially now that increasing power of AI chips has also led to enormous thermal problems. Scaling Single-Crystal Diamond for Chips | Martin Roscheisen | CarbonSemi 2026 - YouTube Watch On What makes Diamond Foundry’s 200mm SCD wafer different from other lab-grown diamonds is that it’s created as a high-quality single-crystal piece instead of a polycrystalline gem. Although the former is difficult to manufacture, it is what allows diamond to become an extreme efficient thermal conductor while simultaneously retaining its electrical insulating properties — this efficiency should help cut down on hotspots, making SCDs an excellent solution for AI chip cooling.The company also showed in a graph that it is now thought possible to create a D300 SCD wafer before 2030, matching the size of the wafers used in leading node processes. However, it should be noted that the sample shown by the company remains unpolished, meaning it still needs to go through some processes to make it suitable for chipmakers.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: (Image credit: Diamond Foundry)Although the company was founded in 2012, it also acknowledged the work of scientists who have been chipping away at the scale problem of SCDs since the early 2000s. “This is one of those milestones that once seemed almost impossible. Hundreds of DF engineers, scientists, and technicians contributed to us getting here. It is the accumulated result of countless experiments, failures, inventions, rebuilt machines, and insights over more than a decade,” Diamond Foundry CEO Martin Roscheisen said.“Stefan and Martin pursued this goal for 25 years. There are very few examples in technology of someone sticking to a really hard scientific challenge with that level of perseverance. They kept going when the prevailing view was that single‑crystal diamond simply could not be made at this scale. Today, the perseverance shows as the first-ever D200mm single‑crystal diamond. And best of all, it makes D300mm predictable as well.” You may like Diamond-infused watercooling coldplates for 2,300W Nvidia Rubin drop temps by up to 22C Hot Chips 2026: Intel Xeon 7 'Diamond Rapids' comes with up to 256 P-cores, 1.28 GB of last-level cache Hot Chips 2026: Cerebras lays out the future of wafer-scale AI Image 1 of 2 (Image credit: Diamond Foundry) (Image credit: Diamond Foundry) Image 1 of 2 View Original Image 2 of 2 View Original Diamond Foundry isn’t the only company that has identified the potential of lab-grown diamonds for semiconductor cooling. Akash Systems secured $18.2 million in CHIPS Act funding in 2024 to produce Gallium Nitride fused with synthetic diamond, which it claims will reduce temperatures by 20 degrees C. The De Beers Group, which is known for its diamond mines in Africa, is also building a copper-plated diamond composite material aimed at improving cooling efficiency for AI, high-performance computing, and GaN RF devices. Even Frore Systems, which is known for its solid-state cooler, is diving into diamond-infused watercooling cold plates for Nvidia’s next-generation AI GPUs. items.titleZh: Diamond Foundry 制造出全球首块 200mm 单晶金刚石晶圆
items.descriptionZh:
金刚石因热导率极高而被视为极具潜力的散热材料，其导热能力估计至少是铜的五倍。专注于实验室培育金刚石的 Diamond Foundry 宣布推出全球首个 200mm 单晶金刚石（SCD）晶圆，并称“单晶金刚石已进入晶圆级时代”。200mm 大致相当于半导体晶圆厂用于成熟制程的晶圆尺寸，这一进展旨在推动单晶金刚石规模化制造，用于半导体冷却，尤其是应对 AI 芯片功耗上升带来的严峻散热问题。

该晶圆的特殊之处在于，它不是多晶宝石，而是高质量单晶金刚石。单晶金刚石制造难度很高，但正因如此，它既能成为极高效的热导体，又能保持电绝缘性。这种组合有助于减少芯片热点，使单晶金刚石成为 AI 芯片冷却的潜在优秀方案。Diamond Foundry 还展示了一张路线图，认为在 2030 年前有望制造出 D300 单晶金刚石晶圆，从而匹配先进制程所用晶圆尺寸。不过，公司展示的样品尚未抛光，仍需经过后续工艺才能适合芯片制造商使用。

Diamond Foundry 成立于 2012 年，但公司也承认，科学家自 2000 年代初以来一直在攻克单晶金刚石的尺寸放大难题。CEO Martin Roscheisen 表示，这是一个曾看似几乎不可能的里程碑，数百名工程师、科学家和技术人员经过十多年的大量实验、失败、发明、设备重建和洞察积累才走到这一步。他还提到，Stefan 和 Martin 为这一目标坚持了 25 年，在主流观点认为单晶金刚石无法做到这种规模时仍持续投入；如今首个 D200mm 单晶金刚石问世，并使 D300mm 变得可预测。

Diamond Foundry 并非唯一看好实验室培育金刚石用于半导体冷却的公司。Akash Systems 于 2024 年获得 1820 万美元《芯片法案》资金，用于生产与合成金刚石融合的氮化镓材料，并声称可将温度降低 20 摄氏度。以非洲钻石矿闻名的 De Beers Group 也在开发铜镀金刚石复合材料，目标是提升 AI、高性能计算和 GaN 射频器件的冷却效率。以固态散热器闻名的 Frore Systems 也在研发面向 Nvidia 下一代 AI GPU 的金刚石注入式水冷冷板。整体来看，单晶金刚石晶圆的规模化进展可能为高功率 AI 芯片散热开辟新的材料路径，但从样品到量产、抛光和与芯片制造流程整合仍需验证。

items.title: Two Chinese companies cleared to buy banned Nvidia AI chips have empty offices and unknown addresses
items.description: The offices for New Matrix and Maginfra, both approved to receive H200 chips, appear abandoned, and people in the buildings say they're unfamiliar with the companies or have never seen anyone working there.
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 1 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter An investigation has found that addresses for two Chinese companies approved to purchase Nvidia H200 chips led to empty offices, and the receptionists at the buildings were unfamiliar with them. According to The New York Times, these companies didn’t just have empty offices; their executives are often linked to other firms sanctioned by the United States for working with and providing advanced technology to the Chinese military.This news has revealed concerns that the U.S. Department of Commerce is simply rubber-stamping GPU export license applications instead of scrutinizing each one for potential links to Beijing. “I have a ton of concerns that neither the Commerce Department or Nvidia is doing the due diligence needed to ensure that the licensing terms are being followed,” former China director for the White House National Security Council Liza Tobin told the publication.Many of these approved companies include well-known entities like Baidu, BYD, Tesla Shanghai, as well as ZTE, which has previously been blacklisted from the U.S. market, Alibaba, Tencent, and ByteDance. However, the outfit’s investigation also revealed approval for two relatively unknown firms: New Matrix and Maginfra. The offices for both companies were empty shells with some office furniture, and people working nearby said they’d never heard of the company or seen anyone go to the deserted spaces.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: The New Matrix website also reportedly did not contain any information about its owners or its history, although public company records reveal that it was founded by Li Bin, who, along with two other primary owners, are connected to Wise Road, a Chinese private equity firm sanctioned by the U.S. for helping Beijing acquire sensitive chip technologies. Furthermore, Mr. Li chairs Tsinghua Unigroup, a tech conglomerate partly owned by the Chinese government, and owns New H3C Semiconductor Technologies, which has also been added to the Commerce Department’s Entity List for cooperating with the Chinese military.Maginfra, on the other hand, is suspected of being linked to Inspur, which Washington has blacklisted since 2023 for supporting the People’s Liberation Army, with both companies sharing personnel, patents, and a similar government ownership structure. These two firms aren’t listed as the final users of Nvidia’s AI chips, though. Instead, they’re supposed to assemble them into AI servers, which would then be forwarded to a final user, although it’s unclear who their customers are. You may like Investigative report details how export-restricted Nvidia AI chips reach China Illegal Nvidia Blackwell Ultra B300 GPUs found inside state-owned China Telecom's network Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang may have been the target of a spy plot through 'Chinese intelligence asset,' report claims Aside from these questionable non-entities, another company that received a license to purchase H200 GPUs has some suspicious links. Zhejiang Yindun Cloud Technology’s executives are reportedly related to the founder of Range Intelligent Computing Technology Group, a data center operator that has sold compute capacity to Chinese military contractors. It’s also reportedly partly operating out of a Range data center.President Donald Trump banned the export of Nvidia AI GPUs in April 2025, even those customized to meet the performance ceiling Washington set for AI processors. The president reversed the decision late last year in exchange for a 25% cut of the sale, but it still took more than eight months for the first H200 shipments to arrive in China. Beijing’s refusal to give Chinese tech companies the green light to buy the chips for the first few months of the year caused the delay. But once China lifted its import ban on Nvidia chips, several Chinese companies applied for licenses to buy them, and The New York Times reported that around two dozen firms have already received approval, including these questionable ones.Stay On the Cutting Edge: Get the Tom's Hardware NewsletterGet Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.Contact me with news and offers from other Future brandsReceive email from us on behalf of our trusted partners or sponsors Follow Tom's Hardware on Google News, or add us as a preferred source, to get our latest news, analysis, & reviews in your feeds.
items.author: Jowi Morales
items.titleZh: 两家获准购买被禁英伟达AI芯片的中国公司办公室空置、地址不明
items.descriptionZh:
《纽约时报》的一项调查显示，两家获准购买英伟达H200 AI芯片的中国公司注册地址竟是空壳办公室，办公楼前台甚至不熟悉这些公司。调查还发现，这些公司的高管往往与因向中国军方提供先进技术或合作而遭美国制裁的企业有关联。这一事件引发外界担忧：美国商务部在审批GPU出口许可证时可能只是“盖章放行”，没有逐项审查申请方与北京或中国军方的潜在联系。美国国家安全委员会前中国事务主任Liza Tobin表示，她非常担心商务部和英伟达都没有做足尽职调查，以确保许可条款得到遵守。

报道指出，获批公司中包括百度、比亚迪、特斯拉上海、曾被美国市场列入黑名单的中兴，以及阿里巴巴、腾讯、字节跳动等知名企业；但调查重点落在两家相对不知名的公司New Matrix和Maginfra上。两家公司的办公室只有部分办公家具，附近人员称从未听说过这些公司，也没见过有人进入这些空置空间。New Matrix网站没有所有者或公司历史信息；公开记录显示其由李滨创立，李滨及其他两名主要所有者与Wise Road有关，而Wise Road是一家因帮助北京获取敏感芯片技术而被美国制裁的中国私募股权公司。李滨还担任部分国有的科技集团清华紫光董事长，并拥有New H3C Semiconductor Technologies，该公司也因与中国军方合作被列入美国商务部实体清单。Maginfra则被怀疑与浪潮有关；浪潮自2023年起因支持中国人民解放军被华盛顿列入黑名单，两家公司共享人员、专利和类似的政府所有权结构。

更关键的是，New Matrix和Maginfra并非英伟达AI芯片的最终用户，而是被批准将芯片组装成AI服务器，再转交给最终用户，但其客户身份并不清楚。这暴露出出口管制中“最终用户”和“最终用途”审查的漏洞：即使芯片不直接售给受限实体，也可能通过服务器集成商和中间环节流入受关注对象。另一家获准购买H200的公司浙江银盾云科技也被指存在可疑关联，其高管与Range Intelligent Computing Technology Group创始人有关，后者是一家数据中心运营商，曾向中国军方承包商出售算力，浙江银盾云据称部分在Range的数据中心运营。

政策背景方面，美国总统特朗普于2025年4月禁止出口英伟达AI GPU，包括为满足华盛顿设定的性能上限而定制的处理器；随后又以抽取25%销售分成的方式逆转决定，但首批H200运抵中国仍耗时八个多月。报道将延迟部分归因于北京在年初数月拒绝为中国科技公司购买这些芯片开绿灯；在中国解除英伟达芯片进口禁令后，多家中国企业申请许可，约二十多家公司已获批准，其中就包括上述存在问题的公司。

从技术角度看，H200属于英伟达面向数据中心的高端AI加速器，配备高带宽内存，适合大模型训练和推理，因此成为出口管制重点。原文并未披露H200的具体性能参数或与其他芯片的量化对比数据，所以无法据此给出详细性能比较；但其受管制核心在于高算力和高带宽可显著提升大规模AI计算能力。此次调查的创新点不在芯片技术本身，而在于揭示出口许可执行机制的风险：在政策反复、审批加速和商业利益驱动下，许可证审查可能流于形式，导致受限制的高端AI芯片通过空壳公司、服务器组装商和复杂股权关系规避管制。其影响涉及美国出口管制有效性、英伟达合规压力、中国云厂商和AI企业获取算力的渠道，以及美国商务部是否应加强对最终用户、最终用途和关联交易的审查。

items.title: PC's with 64GB of RAM plummet 18% as memory prices soar
items.description: CPU-Z data reveals PC memory capacity is dropping for the first time ever. Driven by skyrocketing AI DRAM prices, 64GB RAM adoption plummeted 18% YoY.
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 6 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter The latest CPU-Z hardware survey data shows 32GB and 64GB memory configurations down 2.5% and 18% year on year, respectively. The driving factor is no mystery: High-capacity memory has become a luxury in modern PC builds. The AI rush is still gobbling up the global DRAM supply, so prices for the best RAM options across DDR4 and DDR5 have gone through the roof.If you are not familiar with CPU-Z, it is a free program that gives you a detailed breakdown of the hardware inside your system. It only tracks systems where it is actually installed and running, so it does not report monthly retail sales figures. Do not take the data as sales figures in any sense. They represent CPU-Z's active user base.32GB and 16GB are common configurations that have grown over the years. According to the gathered data, 32GB configurations lead CPU-Z's user base with a 37.2% share, with 16GB configurations close behind at 33%. Not a surprise, really, since applications and games have grown more memory-intensive. 16GB has been the baseline for a long time now, and 32GB is now the sweet spot for many people, even gamers.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: On the flip side, 8GB configurations have been steadily declining. They make up only 11% of the surveyed systems. 8GB systems are rare nowadays. You may still find them in legacy systems, basic office machines, or extremely budget-limited builds where performance takes a backseat. Meanwhile, higher-end configurations, including 64GB and 24GB, are still in the minority at 7.3% and 2.3%, respectively.Fresh stats from CPU-Z! 🔎 For the first time ever, RAM capacity on PCs has declined year-over-year : -2.5% for 32 GB and -18% for 64 GB! https://t.co/ya0soA55bRNovember 6, 2026For the first time, the CPU-Z developer recorded a noticeable decline in higher-capacity configurations. Specifically, 32GB configurations fell 2.5% year over year, while 64GB options dropped a significant 18%. This is likely due to the steep rise in memory prices, which has forced consumers to reconsider the cost-benefit of larger capacities.As the price per gigabyte goes up, buyers are opting for more affordable capacities. Lower-capacity memory kits have seen a somewhat revival. The 16GB configuration, often considered the minimum, has rebounded by 12.9%. Similarly, 8GB configurations, which were previously in sharp decline, grew 5.5%.Interestingly, 24GB configurations also increased by 19.7% and have become a compromise for consumers who need more than 16GB of memory but do not want to spend a lot of money on a premium 32GB memory kit.Stay On the Cutting Edge: Get the Tom's Hardware NewsletterGet Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.Contact me with news and offers from other Future brandsReceive email from us on behalf of our trusted partners or sponsorsHow much money are you willing to spend during the Black Friday sales? The current distribution between DDR4 and DDR5 memory types reveals that DDR4 remains the dominant memory standard at 54.5%. In contrast, DDR5, despite being the latest memory technology, is still in its early adoption phase at 32.9%. DDR4 has been the de facto standard for almost a decade now, so it will take time for DDR5 to overtake it.Nonetheless, the noticeable 6% growth in DDR4 and 2.9% decline in DDR5 suggests budget-conscious consumers are sticking with platforms that still embrace DDR4, such as AMD's Zen 3-powered Ryzen 5000 (codenamed Vermeer) or Intel's 13th Generation Raptor Lake processors. CPU-Z's processor charts show a significant increase in Zen 3 chips, including the Ryzen 7 5700X, Ryzen 5 5600, and Ryzen 5 5500, with figures up to 42.8%, 36.1%, and 67.3%, respectively.Although both DDR4 and DDR5 have increased in price, the former remains slightly more affordable. Companies are supporting the effort too, such as AMD rereleasing the Ryzen 7 5800X3D, vendors restarting DDR4 and DDR4 motherboard production, or Intel preparing rewarmed Raptor Lake Next chips for 2027. items.titleZh: PC's with 64GB of RAM plummet 18% as memory prices soar
items.descriptionZh:
CPU-Z最新硬件调查显示，PC内存容量配置出现罕见逆转：32GB和64GB配置同比分别下降2.5%和18%，这是CPU-Z开发者首次记录到高容量内存配置的明显回落。调查同时显示，32GB仍是CPU-Z活跃用户中最主流的配置，占比37.2%；16GB紧随其后，占33%；8GB占11%；64GB和24GB分别占7.3%和2.3%。需要说明的是，CPU-Z是免费硬件信息工具，只统计安装并运行该程序的系统，反映的是其活跃用户硬件分布，而非零售销量数据。

这一变化的背景是AI热潮持续消耗全球DRAM供应，导致DDR4和DDR5内存价格大幅上涨，高容量内存套件在PC装机中逐渐成为“奢侈品”。当每GB内存价格上升时，消费者开始重新评估大容量配置的性价比，转向更 affordable 的容量选择。于是，原本持续萎缩的低容量配置出现反弹：16GB同比增长12.9%，8GB增长5.5%；24GB配置则同比增长19.7%，成为需要超过16GB、但不愿为32GB高端套件支付高溢价的用户的折中方案。8GB系统目前主要用于老旧设备、基础办公机或极度受限的预算装机；16GB仍是长期以来的入门基线；32GB则是许多用户和游戏玩家的“甜点”容量，但其同比增长受到价格压制；64GB等高端配置仍属少数。

从内存代际看，DDR4仍以54.5%的份额占据主导，DDR5尽管是最新技术，仍处于早期采用阶段，份额为32.9%。数据还显示DDR4录得6%的增长，而DDR5下降2.9%，说明预算敏感型消费者更倾向留在仍支持DDR4的平台上，例如AMD Zen 3架构的Ryzen 5000系列（Vermeer）或Intel第13代Raptor Lake处理器。CPU-Z处理器图表中，Zen 3芯片显著增长：Ryzen 7 5700X、Ryzen 5 5600和Ryzen 5 5500分别增长42.8%、36.1%和67.3%。这背后的技术逻辑在于，DDR4作为成熟标准已部署近十年，主板和内存成本相对更低；DDR5虽具备更高带宽和能效潜力，但在价格敏感期，平台整体成本会显著影响用户选择。

产业层面，这一趋势正在延长DDR4平台的生命周期：AMD重新推出Ryzen 7 5800X3D，厂商重启DDR4内存及DDR4主板生产，Intel也被报道准备在2027年推出Raptor Lake Next等延续DDR4兼容性的产品。对应用场景而言，基础办公和老旧系统继续停留在8GB；主流游戏和日常多任务以16GB为基线；32GB仍是游戏、内容和多任务用户的理想容量，但增长受内存价格抑制；64GB及以上主要面向专业创作、虚拟化和工作站用户。总体来看，AI驱动的DRAM供应紧张正在通过价格传导改变PC装机结构，短期内可能放缓DDR5普及和高容量内存渗透，并推动DDR4平台与24GB等折中容量继续存在。

And best of all, it makes D300mm predictable as well.” You may like Diamond-infused watercooling coldplates for 2,300W Nvidia Rubin drop temps by up to 22C Hot Chips 2026: Intel Xeon 7 'Diamond Rapids' comes with up to 256 P-cores, 1.28 GB of last-level cache Hot Chips 2026: Cerebras lays out the future of wafer-scale AI Image 1 of 2 (Image credit: Diamond Foundry) (Image credit: Diamond Foundry) Image 1 of 2 View Original Image 2 of 2 View Original Diamond Foundry isn’t the only company that has identified the potential of lab-grown diamonds for semiconductor cooling. Akash Systems secured $18.2 million in CHIPS Act funding in 2024 to produce Gallium Nitride fused with synthetic diamond, which it claims will reduce temperatures by 20 degrees C. The De Beers Group, which is known for its diamond mines in Africa, is also building a copper-plated diamond composite material aimed at improving cooling efficiency for AI, high-performance computing, and GaN RF devices. Even Frore Systems, which is known for its solid-state cooler, is diving into diamond-infused watercooling cold plates for Nvidia’s next-generation AI GPUs. history.author: Jowi Morales
history.titleZh: Diamond Foundry 制造出全球首块 200mm 单晶金刚石晶圆
history.descriptionZh:
金刚石因热导率极高而被视为极具潜力的散热材料，其导热能力估计至少是铜的五倍。专注于实验室培育金刚石的 Diamond Foundry 宣布推出全球首个 200mm 单晶金刚石（SCD）晶圆，并称“单晶金刚石已进入晶圆级时代”。200mm 大致相当于半导体晶圆厂用于成熟制程的晶圆尺寸，这一进展旨在推动单晶金刚石规模化制造，用于半导体冷却，尤其是应对 AI 芯片功耗上升带来的严峻散热问题。

该晶圆的特殊之处在于，它不是多晶宝石，而是高质量单晶金刚石。单晶金刚石制造难度很高，但正因如此，它既能成为极高效的热导体，又能保持电绝缘性。这种组合有助于减少芯片热点，使单晶金刚石成为 AI 芯片冷却的潜在优秀方案。Diamond Foundry 还展示了一张路线图，认为在 2030 年前有望制造出 D300 单晶金刚石晶圆，从而匹配先进制程所用晶圆尺寸。不过，公司展示的样品尚未抛光，仍需经过后续工艺才能适合芯片制造商使用。

Diamond Foundry 成立于 2012 年，但公司也承认，科学家自 2000 年代初以来一直在攻克单晶金刚石的尺寸放大难题。CEO Martin Roscheisen 表示，这是一个曾看似几乎不可能的里程碑，数百名工程师、科学家和技术人员经过十多年的大量实验、失败、发明、设备重建和洞察积累才走到这一步。他还提到，Stefan 和 Martin 为这一目标坚持了 25 年，在主流观点认为单晶金刚石无法做到这种规模时仍持续投入；如今首个 D200mm 单晶金刚石问世，并使 D300mm 变得可预测。

Diamond Foundry 并非唯一看好实验室培育金刚石用于半导体冷却的公司。Akash Systems 于 2024 年获得 1820 万美元《芯片法案》资金，用于生产与合成金刚石融合的氮化镓材料，并声称可将温度降低 20 摄氏度。以非洲钻石矿闻名的 De Beers Group 也在开发铜镀金刚石复合材料，目标是提升 AI、高性能计算和 GaN 射频器件的冷却效率。以固态散热器闻名的 Frore Systems 也在研发面向 Nvidia 下一代 AI GPU 的金刚石注入式水冷冷板。整体来看，单晶金刚石晶圆的规模化进展可能为高功率 AI 芯片散热开辟新的材料路径，但从样品到量产、抛光和与芯片制造流程整合仍需验证。

history.title: Two Chinese companies cleared to buy banned Nvidia AI chips have empty offices and unknown addresses
history.description: The offices for New Matrix and Maginfra, both approved to receive H200 chips, appear abandoned, and people in the buildings say they're unfamiliar with the companies or have never seen anyone working there.
history.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 1 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter An investigation has found that addresses for two Chinese companies approved to purchase Nvidia H200 chips led to empty offices, and the receptionists at the buildings were unfamiliar with them. According to The New York Times, these companies didn’t just have empty offices; their executives are often linked to other firms sanctioned by the United States for working with and providing advanced technology to the Chinese military.This news has revealed concerns that the U.S. Department of Commerce is simply rubber-stamping GPU export license applications instead of scrutinizing each one for potential links to Beijing. “I have a ton of concerns that neither the Commerce Department or Nvidia is doing the due diligence needed to ensure that the licensing terms are being followed,” former China director for the White House National Security Council Liza Tobin told the publication.Many of these approved companies include well-known entities like Baidu, BYD, Tesla Shanghai, as well as ZTE, which has previously been blacklisted from the U.S. market, Alibaba, Tencent, and ByteDance. However, the outfit’s investigation also revealed approval for two relatively unknown firms: New Matrix and Maginfra. The offices for both companies were empty shells with some office furniture, and people working nearby said they’d never heard of the company or seen anyone go to the deserted spaces.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: The New Matrix website also reportedly did not contain any information about its owners or its history, although public company records reveal that it was founded by Li Bin, who, along with two other primary owners, are connected to Wise Road, a Chinese private equity firm sanctioned by the U.S. for helping Beijing acquire sensitive chip technologies. Furthermore, Mr. Li chairs Tsinghua Unigroup, a tech conglomerate partly owned by the Chinese government, and owns New H3C Semiconductor Technologies, which has also been added to the Commerce Department’s Entity List for cooperating with the Chinese military.Maginfra, on the other hand, is suspected of being linked to Inspur, which Washington has blacklisted since 2023 for supporting the People’s Liberation Army, with both companies sharing personnel, patents, and a similar government ownership structure. These two firms aren’t listed as the final users of Nvidia’s AI chips, though. Instead, they’re supposed to assemble them into AI servers, which would then be forwarded to a final user, although it’s unclear who their customers are. You may like Investigative report details how export-restricted Nvidia AI chips reach China Illegal Nvidia Blackwell Ultra B300 GPUs found inside state-owned China Telecom's network Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang may have been the target of a spy plot through 'Chinese intelligence asset,' report claims Aside from these questionable non-entities, another company that received a license to purchase H200 GPUs has some suspicious links. Zhejiang Yindun Cloud Technology’s executives are reportedly related to the founder of Range Intelligent Computing Technology Group, a data center operator that has sold compute capacity to Chinese military contractors. It’s also reportedly partly operating out of a Range data center.President Donald Trump banned the export of Nvidia AI GPUs in April 2025, even those customized to meet the performance ceiling Washington set for AI processors. The president reversed the decision late last year in exchange for a 25% cut of the sale, but it still took more than eight months for the first H200 shipments to arrive in China. Beijing’s refusal to give Chinese tech companies the green light to buy the chips for the first few months of the year caused the delay. But once China lifted its import ban on Nvidia chips, several Chinese companies applied for licenses to buy them, and The New York Times reported that around two dozen firms have already received approval, including these questionable ones.Stay On the Cutting Edge: Get the Tom's Hardware NewsletterGet Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.Contact me with news and offers from other Future brandsReceive email from us on behalf of our trusted partners or sponsors Follow Tom's Hardware on Google News, or add us as a preferred source, to get our latest news, analysis, & reviews in your feeds.
history.author: Jowi Morales
history.titleZh: 两家获准购买被禁英伟达AI芯片的中国公司办公室空置、地址不明
history.descriptionZh:
《纽约时报》的一项调查显示，两家获准购买英伟达H200 AI芯片的中国公司注册地址竟是空壳办公室，办公楼前台甚至不熟悉这些公司。调查还发现，这些公司的高管往往与因向中国军方提供先进技术或合作而遭美国制裁的企业有关联。这一事件引发外界担忧：美国商务部在审批GPU出口许可证时可能只是“盖章放行”，没有逐项审查申请方与北京或中国军方的潜在联系。美国国家安全委员会前中国事务主任Liza Tobin表示，她非常担心商务部和英伟达都没有做足尽职调查，以确保许可条款得到遵守。

报道指出，获批公司中包括百度、比亚迪、特斯拉上海、曾被美国市场列入黑名单的中兴，以及阿里巴巴、腾讯、字节跳动等知名企业；但调查重点落在两家相对不知名的公司New Matrix和Maginfra上。两家公司的办公室只有部分办公家具，附近人员称从未听说过这些公司，也没见过有人进入这些空置空间。New Matrix网站没有所有者或公司历史信息；公开记录显示其由李滨创立，李滨及其他两名主要所有者与Wise Road有关，而Wise Road是一家因帮助北京获取敏感芯片技术而被美国制裁的中国私募股权公司。李滨还担任部分国有的科技集团清华紫光董事长，并拥有New H3C Semiconductor Technologies，该公司也因与中国军方合作被列入美国商务部实体清单。Maginfra则被怀疑与浪潮有关；浪潮自2023年起因支持中国人民解放军被华盛顿列入黑名单，两家公司共享人员、专利和类似的政府所有权结构。

更关键的是，New Matrix和Maginfra并非英伟达AI芯片的最终用户，而是被批准将芯片组装成AI服务器，再转交给最终用户，但其客户身份并不清楚。这暴露出出口管制中“最终用户”和“最终用途”审查的漏洞：即使芯片不直接售给受限实体，也可能通过服务器集成商和中间环节流入受关注对象。另一家获准购买H200的公司浙江银盾云科技也被指存在可疑关联，其高管与Range Intelligent Computing Technology Group创始人有关，后者是一家数据中心运营商，曾向中国军方承包商出售算力，浙江银盾云据称部分在Range的数据中心运营。

政策背景方面，美国总统特朗普于2025年4月禁止出口英伟达AI GPU，包括为满足华盛顿设定的性能上限而定制的处理器；随后又以抽取25%销售分成的方式逆转决定，但首批H200运抵中国仍耗时八个多月。报道将延迟部分归因于北京在年初数月拒绝为中国科技公司购买这些芯片开绿灯；在中国解除英伟达芯片进口禁令后，多家中国企业申请许可，约二十多家公司已获批准，其中就包括上述存在问题的公司。

从技术角度看，H200属于英伟达面向数据中心的高端AI加速器，配备高带宽内存，适合大模型训练和推理，因此成为出口管制重点。原文并未披露H200的具体性能参数或与其他芯片的量化对比数据，所以无法据此给出详细性能比较；但其受管制核心在于高算力和高带宽可显著提升大规模AI计算能力。此次调查的创新点不在芯片技术本身，而在于揭示出口许可执行机制的风险：在政策反复、审批加速和商业利益驱动下，许可证审查可能流于形式，导致受限制的高端AI芯片通过空壳公司、服务器组装商和复杂股权关系规避管制。其影响涉及美国出口管制有效性、英伟达合规压力、中国云厂商和AI企业获取算力的渠道，以及美国商务部是否应加强对最终用户、最终用途和关联交易的审查。

history.title: PC's with 64GB of RAM plummet 18% as memory prices soar
history.description: CPU-Z data reveals PC memory capacity is dropping for the first time ever. Driven by skyrocketing AI DRAM prices, 64GB RAM adoption plummeted 18% YoY.
history.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 6 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter The latest CPU-Z hardware survey data shows 32GB and 64GB memory configurations down 2.5% and 18% year on year, respectively. The driving factor is no mystery: High-capacity memory has become a luxury in modern PC builds. The AI rush is still gobbling up the global DRAM supply, so prices for the best RAM options across DDR4 and DDR5 have gone through the roof.If you are not familiar with CPU-Z, it is a free program that gives you a detailed breakdown of the hardware inside your system. It only tracks systems where it is actually installed and running, so it does not report monthly retail sales figures. Do not take the data as sales figures in any sense. They represent CPU-Z's active user base.32GB and 16GB are common configurations that have grown over the years. According to the gathered data, 32GB configurations lead CPU-Z's user base with a 37.2% share, with 16GB configurations close behind at 33%. Not a surprise, really, since applications and games have grown more memory-intensive. 16GB has been the baseline for a long time now, and 32GB is now the sweet spot for many people, even gamers.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: On the flip side, 8GB configurations have been steadily declining. They make up only 11% of the surveyed systems. 8GB systems are rare nowadays. You may still find them in legacy systems, basic office machines, or extremely budget-limited builds where performance takes a backseat. Meanwhile, higher-end configurations, including 64GB and 24GB, are still in the minority at 7.3% and 2.3%, respectively.Fresh stats from CPU-Z! 🔎 For the first time ever, RAM capacity on PCs has declined year-over-year : -2.5% for 32 GB and -18% for 64 GB! https://t.co/ya0soA55bRNovember 6, 2026For the first time, the CPU-Z developer recorded a noticeable decline in higher-capacity configurations. Specifically, 32GB configurations fell 2.5% year over year, while 64GB options dropped a significant 18%. This is likely due to the steep rise in memory prices, which has forced consumers to reconsider the cost-benefit of larger capacities.As the price per gigabyte goes up, buyers are opting for more affordable capacities. Lower-capacity memory kits have seen a somewhat revival. The 16GB configuration, often considered the minimum, has rebounded by 12.9%. Similarly, 8GB configurations, which were previously in sharp decline, grew 5.5%.Interestingly, 24GB configurations also increased by 19.7% and have become a compromise for consumers who need more than 16GB of memory but do not want to spend a lot of money on a premium 32GB memory kit.Stay On the Cutting Edge: Get the Tom's Hardware NewsletterGet Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.Contact me with news and offers from other Future brandsReceive email from us on behalf of our trusted partners or sponsorsHow much money are you willing to spend during the Black Friday sales? The current distribution between DDR4 and DDR5 memory types reveals that DDR4 remains the dominant memory standard at 54.5%. In contrast, DDR5, despite being the latest memory technology, is still in its early adoption phase at 32.9%. DDR4 has been the de facto standard for almost a decade now, so it will take time for DDR5 to overtake it.Nonetheless, the noticeable 6% growth in DDR4 and 2.9% decline in DDR5 suggests budget-conscious consumers are sticking with platforms that still embrace DDR4, such as AMD's Zen 3-powered Ryzen 5000 (codenamed Vermeer) or Intel's 13th Generation Raptor Lake processors. CPU-Z's processor charts show a significant increase in Zen 3 chips, including the Ryzen 7 5700X, Ryzen 5 5600, and Ryzen 5 5500, with figures up to 42.8%, 36.1%, and 67.3%, respectively.Although both DDR4 and DDR5 have increased in price, the former remains slightly more affordable. Companies are supporting the effort too, such as AMD rereleasing the Ryzen 7 5800X3D, vendors restarting DDR4 and DDR4 motherboard production, or Intel preparing rewarmed Raptor Lake Next chips for 2027. history.author: Zhiye Liu
history.titleZh: PC's with 64GB of RAM plummet 18% as memory prices soar
history.descriptionZh:
CPU-Z最新硬件调查显示，PC内存容量配置出现罕见逆转：32GB和64GB配置同比分别下降2.5%和18%，这是CPU-Z开发者首次记录到高容量内存配置的明显回落。调查同时显示，32GB仍是CPU-Z活跃用户中最主流的配置，占比37.2%；16GB紧随其后，占33%；8GB占11%；64GB和24GB分别占7.3%和2.3%。需要说明的是，CPU-Z是免费硬件信息工具，只统计安装并运行该程序的系统，反映的是其活跃用户硬件分布，而非零售销量数据。

这一变化的背景是AI热潮持续消耗全球DRAM供应，导致DDR4和DDR5内存价格大幅上涨，高容量内存套件在PC装机中逐渐成为“奢侈品”。当每GB内存价格上升时，消费者开始重新评估大容量配置的性价比，转向更 affordable 的容量选择。于是，原本持续萎缩的低容量配置出现反弹：16GB同比增长12.9%，8GB增长5.5%；24GB配置则同比增长19.7%，成为需要超过16GB、但不愿为32GB高端套件支付高溢价的用户的折中方案。8GB系统目前主要用于老旧设备、基础办公机或极度受限的预算装机；16GB仍是长期以来的入门基线；32GB则是许多用户和游戏玩家的“甜点”容量，但其同比增长受到价格压制；64GB等高端配置仍属少数。

从内存代际看，DDR4仍以54.5%的份额占据主导，DDR5尽管是最新技术，仍处于早期采用阶段，份额为32.9%。数据还显示DDR4录得6%的增长，而DDR5下降2.9%，说明预算敏感型消费者更倾向留在仍支持DDR4的平台上，例如AMD Zen 3架构的Ryzen 5000系列（Vermeer）或Intel第13代Raptor Lake处理器。CPU-Z处理器图表中，Zen 3芯片显著增长：Ryzen 7 5700X、Ryzen 5 5600和Ryzen 5 5500分别增长42.8%、36.1%和67.3%。这背后的技术逻辑在于，DDR4作为成熟标准已部署近十年，主板和内存成本相对更低；DDR5虽具备更高带宽和能效潜力，但在价格敏感期，平台整体成本会显著影响用户选择。

产业层面，这一趋势正在延长DDR4平台的生命周期：AMD重新推出Ryzen 7 5800X3D，厂商重启DDR4内存及DDR4主板生产，Intel也被报道准备在2027年推出Raptor Lake Next等延续DDR4兼容性的产品。对应用场景而言，基础办公和老旧系统继续停留在8GB；主流游戏和日常多任务以16GB为基线；32GB仍是游戏、内容和多任务用户的理想容量，但增长受内存价格抑制；64GB及以上主要面向专业创作、虚拟化和工作站用户。总体来看，AI驱动的DRAM供应紧张正在通过价格传导改变PC装机结构，短期内可能放缓DDR5普及和高容量内存渗透，并推动DDR4平台与24GB等折中容量继续存在。
